sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是“每日新闻”。

sentences.en: The James Webb Space Telescope has revolutionized the way that we see the universe.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·韦布空间望远镜彻底改变了我们看待宇宙的方式。

sentences.en: But naming that telescope sparked an unexpected firestorm within NASA and the wider scientific community.
sentences.zh: 但给这台望远镜命名，在NASA以及更广泛的科学界引发了一场意想不到的风暴。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Michael Powell, tells the story of the astrophysicist whose quest to end the controversy only made it worse.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事迈克尔·鲍威尔将讲述一位天体物理学家的故事，他试图平息这场争议，却让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: It's Friday, May 19th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月19日，星期五。

sentences.en: Michael, welcome to the studio.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，欢迎来到演播室。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: I want to start by talking about your beat.
sentences.zh: 我想从你的报道领域开始聊起。

sentences.en: Because your beat did not exist even five years ago, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你的这个领域在五年前甚至都不存在，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a new beat, and I think it's worth explaining what exactly it is.
sentences.zh: 这是一个新的领域，我觉得有必要解释一下它到底是什么。

sentences.en: It's not easy to describe.
sentences.zh: 这并不容易描述。

sentences.en: I colloquially think of it as the third rail beat.
sentences.zh: 我通常把它比作“第三轨”领域。

sentences.en: Do not touch this rail beat.
sentences.zh: 也就是“绝对碰不得”的领域。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But essentially looking at free expression, free speech, and intellectual debates very often around ethnicity, race, gender.
sentences.zh: 但本质上是关注言论自由、表达自由，以及经常围绕族裔、种族和性别的知识分子辩论。

sentences.en: So, yeah, all of the hot buttons in our current cultural climate.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，涵盖了我们当前文化氛围中的所有敏感话题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A pretty thorny beat.
sentences.zh: 一个相当棘手的领域。

sentences.en: And just so listeners understand, what actual kinds of stories are we talking about here?
sentences.zh: 为了让听众们明白，我们到底在讨论哪类具体的故事？

sentences.en: The broader landscape is, look, we are in the middle of ferocious battles over book banning, over transgender identity, whether transgender athletes can compete.
sentences.zh: 更广泛的背景是，看吧，我们正处于关于禁书、跨性别身份以及跨性别运动员能否参赛的激烈争论之中。

sentences.en: So, these are the sort of stories that I'm looking at on a regular basis.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些就是我经常关注的故事类型。

sentences.en: Some of those are these kind of broader questions, and then some are because these are the ones that galvanize our attention.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分是这种更广泛的问题，还有一部分是因为这些事情吸引了我们的注意力。

sentences.en: What happens to an individual who finds him or herself caught up in these battles?
sentences.zh: 当一个人发现自己卷入这些争论中时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: And you're here, Michael, to talk about how this kind of a battle came to, of all places, NASA, the nation's premier space agency.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，你今天来这里，是要谈谈这种争论是如何蔓延到偏偏是NASA这个全美顶尖太空机构的。

sentences.en: Recording, going.
sentences.zh: 正在录音，进行中。

sentences.en: So, where does that story start?
sentences.zh: 那么，这个故事是从哪里开始的呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Can you tell me your name and who you are?
sentences.zh: 能告诉我你的名字和你的身份吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Hakeem Olusheyi.
sentences.zh: 我是哈基姆·奥卢谢伊博士。

sentences.en: It starts with this, frankly, very impressive man, Dr. Hakeem Olusheyi.
sentences.zh: 故事要从这位坦率讲非常令人印象深刻的人说起，哈基姆·奥卢谢伊博士。

sentences.en: I am an astrophysicist, and I'm newly a research faculty fellow at Princeton's Plasma Physics Laboratory.
sentences.zh: 我是一名天体物理学家，也是普林斯顿等离子体物理实验室新晋的研究教员。

sentences.en: So, he's a member of the small elite club of black physicists.
sentences.zh: 所以，他是黑人物理学家这个小型精英俱乐部的一员。

sentences.en: In fact, he's the president of the National Society of Black Physicists.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他还是全美黑人物理学家协会的主席。

sentences.en: And he himself comes out of a background that really kind of made it unlikely that you'd ever see him as a scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 他自身的成长背景，按理说几乎不可能让你觉得他会成为一名科学家。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 详细讲讲。

sentences.en: So, we had this kind of itinerant childhood.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们度过了一种可以说是四处流浪的童年。

sentences.en: His father was a drug dealer.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是个毒贩。

sentences.en: His mother had a very tough time of it.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲过得很艰难。

sentences.en: His parents divorced when he was only four years old, and he was never in the same place for more than a few years at a time.
sentences.zh: 在他年仅四岁时父母就离婚了，而且他从来没有在一个地方连续住超过几年。

sentences.en: New Orleans, Los Angeles, Houston.
sentences.zh: 新奥尔良、洛杉矶、休斯敦。

sentences.en: Eventually, his family settles in rural Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 最终，他的家人在密西西比州的农村安顿下来。

sentences.en: When did you first realize you were going to be interested in science?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候第一次意识到自己对科学感兴趣的？

sentences.en: You know, as far as back as I can remember, I was interested in the natural world, and I was also interested in everything that's weird.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，打我有记忆起，我就对自然界感兴趣，而且我对所有古怪的东西也都感兴趣。

sentences.en: And his interest in science came very young.
sentences.zh: 他对科学的兴趣萌生得很早。

sentences.en: When I was 10 years old, I decided that I was going to read our family set of world book encyclopedias from A to Z.
sentences.zh: 在我10岁的时候，我决定把家里的一套《世界图书百科全书》从A到Z读完。

sentences.en: I get to E, and I encounter Albert Einstein in relativity.
sentences.zh: 当我读到E时，我遇到了阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦和相对论。

sentences.en: All right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So, this brings together everything that interested me.
sentences.zh: 这把所有我感兴趣的东西都结合在了一起。

sentences.en: So, I vowed to teach myself relativity, never thinking that one day I'd be a scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 于是我发誓要自学相对论，从没想过有一天我会成为一名科学家。

sentences.en: And his mom sees this burning desire to learn in her son.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲看到了儿子这种强烈的求知欲。

sentences.en: She does the best she can to encourage it.
sentences.zh: 她尽其所能地去鼓励这种求知欲。

sentences.en: So, my mother did factory work.
sentences.zh: 我的母亲是一名工厂工人。

sentences.en: So, there were times, you know, she'd work 3D 11, 11 to 7.
sentences.zh: 所以有时候，你知道的，她会上下午三点到十一点、晚上十一点到早晨七点的班。

sentences.en: And there were, you know, sometimes on certain weeks, based on her shift, I wouldn't see her at all.
sentences.zh: 有时候，在某些周，根据她的轮班情况，我甚至完全见不到她。

sentences.en: But I'd come home, and on the dining room table, she had gone to either the Laurel Library or our little library in Heidelberg, Mississippi,
sentences.zh: 但我回到家时，会发现餐桌上放着她从劳雷尔图书馆或者我们密西西比州海德堡的小图书馆借来的书，

sentences.en: and brought two or three books on either Albert Einstein or relativity for me to consume.
sentences.zh: 带了两三本关于阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦或相对论的书让我阅读。

sentences.en: And, you know, I'd get so excited.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我会兴奋得不行。

sentences.en: It was like Christmas for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说就像过圣诞节一样。

sentences.en: And he just had this preternatural ability with mathematics and physics.
sentences.zh: 他在数学和物理方面展现出了惊人的天赋。

sentences.en: He graduates from high school.
sentences.zh: 他从高中毕业。

sentences.en: Then he gets his Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 然后他在斯坦福大学获得了博士学位。

sentences.en: at Stanford University.
sentences.zh: 然后他在斯坦福大学获得了博士学位。

sentences.en: And eventually, he gets a job as a professor at the Florida Institute of Technology.
sentences.zh: 最终，他在佛罗里达理工学院找到了一份教授的工作。

sentences.en: And one day, in 2015, he's reading this online article.
sentences.zh: 有一天，在2015年，他正在读一篇网络文章。

sentences.en: You know, I'm doing my normal, you know, take a break between work and just go get lost on the Internet, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我当时正在做我日常做的事，在工作间隙休息一下，在互联网上闲逛，对吧？

sentences.en: Go down some rabbit hole.
sentences.zh: 陷入某种网络迷宫。

sentences.en: And he comes across this rather stunning story involving NASA's Deep Space Telescope, most powerful such telescope ever made.
sentences.zh: 他偶然看到了一篇相当震撼的故事，内容涉及NASA的深空望远镜，这是有史以来制造的最强大的此类望远镜。

sentences.en: And it's named after James Webb, former administrator of NASA during the whole moon launch effort.
sentences.zh: 它是以詹姆斯·韦布的名字命名的，他曾是NASA在整个登月努力期间的局长。

sentences.en: And the article argues that he is absolutely not deserving of that honor.
sentences.zh: 文章认为他绝对不配得到这份荣誉。

sentences.en: In fact, the title of the article is The Problem with Naming Observatories for Bigots.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这篇文章的标题是《用偏执狂的名字命名天文台的问题》。

sentences.en: Would you mind, kind of in a sense, walk through the accusations?
sentences.zh: 你介意顺着这些指控梳理一下吗？

sentences.en: Like one by one, what's the bill of indictment against James Webb?
sentences.zh: 比如一条一条地看，对詹姆斯·韦布的指控都有哪些？

sentences.en: They were pretty explicit.
sentences.zh: 它们写得很明确。

sentences.en: They said James Webb was a homophobe who ruined the lives and careers of gay federal employees in the 1940s and 50s.
sentences.zh: 他们说詹姆斯·韦布是一个恐同者，在20世纪40和50年代毁掉了同性恋联邦雇员的生活和职业生涯。

sentences.en: That article argued that before coming to NASA, James Webb had led purges of gay employees while at the State Department.
sentences.zh: 那篇文章辩称，詹姆斯·韦布在来到NASA之前，曾在国务院领导过对同性恋雇员的清洗。

sentences.en: And it quotes him saying really inflammatory things about getting rid of gay employees.
sentences.zh: 文章还引用了他关于清除同性恋雇员的极具煽动性的言论。

sentences.en: And the writer, who's a journalist and a physicist, says that this is a sort of moral reckoning.
sentences.zh: 而这位身为记者兼物理学家的作者表示，这是一场道德清算。

sentences.en: That we cannot, in the 21st century, honor a man such as this by putting his name on a space telescope that is going to be used the world round.
sentences.zh: 我们不能在21世纪，通过将这样一个人名字命名一个将在全世界使用的太空望远镜来纪念他。

sentences.en: So, for instance, this journalist writes, it's easy for white male physicists like me to ignore the less savory aspects of our scientific heroes.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，这位记者写道，像我这样的白人男性物理学家很容易忽视我们科学英雄身上那些不太光彩的方面。

sentences.en: But it's long past time we stopped.
sentences.zh: 但我们早该停止这种忽视了。

sentences.en: So James Webb is facing pretty serious allegations of discriminatory behavior that would not seem to make him a great candidate
sentences.zh: 因此，詹姆斯·韦布面临着相当严重的歧视行为指控，这似乎让他无法成为一个理想的人选

sentences.en: to have his name emblazoned on NASA's premier supertelescope.
sentences.zh: 来将他的名字印在NASA顶级的超级望远镜上。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it looks, on the face of it, pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，表面上看，这确实很糟糕。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And what does Hakeem Oluseyi make of these claims?
sentences.zh: 那么哈基姆·奥卢谢伊对这些说法是怎么看的呢？

sentences.en: You know, I'm appalled, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我惊呆了，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm like, oh, you've got to be kidding me.
sentences.zh: 我想，哦，你在开玩笑吧。

sentences.en: The James Webb Space Telescope?
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·韦布空间望远镜？

sentences.en: You know, this is bigger than Hubble is going to be.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这比哈勃望远镜的规模还要大。

sentences.en: Hakeem is completely taken aback.
sentences.zh: 哈基姆完全被震惊了。

sentences.en: He's on a Facebook page with other black, Latino, and gay physicists.
sentences.zh: 他在一个有其他黑人、拉丁裔和同性恋物理学家的Facebook群组里。

sentences.en: Everybody's worked up about this.
sentences.zh: 大家都为这事群情激愤。

sentences.en: I saw people in that Facebook group talking about how they felt about seeing this and how they felt about NASA and their nation.
sentences.zh: 我看到那个Facebook群组里的人在讨论他们看到这个消息时的感受，以及他们对NASA和他们国家的感受。

sentences.en: And what about the youth coming up, right?
sentences.zh: 还有那些初出茅庐的年轻人呢，对吧？

sentences.en: I felt like they, too, would even be more tortured by it, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们甚至会因此受到更大的折磨，对吧？

sentences.en: You're newly coming into this field.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚进入这个领域。

sentences.en: This is the latest, greatest data.
sentences.zh: 这是最新、最棒的数据。

sentences.en: And you have to deal with someone that you feel, you know, literally would hate you and persecute you if they were alive today.
sentences.zh: 而你却不得不去面对这样一个人物，在你看来，如果他今天还活着，他简直会恨你、迫害你。

sentences.en: And there is a request, because he is a prominent physicist, that Hakeem joined them in denouncing this and pushing NASA to do something to change this.
sentences.zh: 由于他是一位杰出的物理学家，有人请求哈基姆加入他们，一同谴责此事并敦促NASA采取行动改变现状。

sentences.en: And that request is basically, take Webb's name off the telescope.
sentences.zh: 这个请求基本上就是，把韦布的名字从望远镜上拿下来。

sentences.en: Off the telescope, yes.
sentences.zh: 从望远镜上拿下来，是的。

sentences.en: And Hakeem gives that some thought.
sentences.zh: 哈基姆对此进行了思考。

sentences.en: So the first thing I do is I decide, let me research this, you know, not deeply, just do a Google search.
sentences.zh: 所以我做的第一件事就是决定，让我研究一下这个，你知道，不用太深入，就做个谷歌搜索。

sentences.en: And I found another article that had been written five, six months earlier by Dan Savage in Seattle that basically said the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我找到了西雅图的丹·萨维奇在五六个月前写的一篇文章，基本上表达了同样的意思。

sentences.en: But I still know that I don't know until I confirm for myself, right?
sentences.zh: 但我仍然明白，在亲自证实之前我并不真正了解情况，对吧？

sentences.en: But I'm certainly sympathetic to it, because if it is true, this is terrible.
sentences.zh: 不过我当然对这种说法表示同情，因为如果这是真的，那就太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And then says to himself, you know, if I'm going to do this, I want to know what the real story is here.
sentences.zh: 然后他对自己说，你知道的，如果我要这么做，我想知道这里真正的故事是什么。

sentences.en: And so?
sentences.zh: 然后呢？

sentences.en: So as fate would have it, he takes a job at NASA.
sentences.zh: 所以命运使然，他在NASA找到了一份工作。

sentences.en: And when he gets there, he goes into the office of some of his higher ups.
sentences.zh: 等他到了那里，他走进了某些高层领导的办公室。

sentences.en: And he says, look, you know, what do we make of this?
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，你知道的，我们该如何看待这件事？

sentences.en: I took it to the head of strategic communications.
sentences.zh: 我把它带到了战略传播主管那里。

sentences.en: And I said, hey, are you aware of this?
sentences.zh: 我说，嘿，你知道这件事吗？

sentences.en: And they said, no.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不知道。

sentences.en: Oh, my goodness.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Let's go talk to Gregory Robinson, who basically led the James Webb Space Telescope to completion.
sentences.zh: 我们去跟格雷戈里·罗宾逊谈谈吧，他基本上是带领詹姆斯·韦布空间望远镜走向完工的人。

sentences.en: He was concerned.
sentences.zh: 他很关切。

sentences.en: He's like, oh, this is not good.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，这可不好。

sentences.en: Let's look into this.
sentences.zh: 我们来查查这件事。

sentences.en: And he said, Hakeem, please send me everything you have.
sentences.zh: 他说，哈基姆，请把你知道的所有东西都发给我。

sentences.en: And so I sent him the two articles.
sentences.zh: 于是我把那两篇文章发给了他。

sentences.en: I sent him the Wikipedia article.
sentences.zh: 我把维基百科的文章发给了他。

sentences.en: And that's all I could find up to that point.
sentences.zh: 这就是我当时能找到的所有资料。

sentences.en: And so I had another meeting with him a week later.
sentences.zh: 一周后我和他又开了一次会。

sentences.en: And he said, Hakeem, you know, this does not provide any actual evidence of what happened.
sentences.zh: 他说，哈基姆，你知道的，这并没有提供任何关于所发生事情的实质证据。

sentences.en: All I see here is accusations.
sentences.zh: 我在这里看到的只有指控。

sentences.en: Would you mind looking into it and finding out what actually happened?
sentences.zh: 你介意调查一下并找出到底发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: And I said, sure, I'd love to, right?
sentences.zh: 我说，当然，我很乐意，对吧？

sentences.en: Because I had the exact same curiosity and I love the research.
sentences.zh: 因为我有着完全一样的好奇心，而且我也热爱研究。

sentences.en: So, you know, that sounds great.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，听起来很棒。

sentences.en: And according to Hakeem, they tell him, would you please take a look at it?
sentences.zh: 根据哈基姆的说法，他们告诉他，能不能请你看一下这个？

sentences.en: So what starts as a kind of personal curiosity about who James Webb really was and what he did is now becoming kind of official business from NASA.
sentences.zh: 因此，最初对詹姆斯·韦布究竟是谁及其所作所为的一种个人好奇，现在正变成NASA的一种官方事务。

sentences.en: Get to the bottom of this.
sentences.zh: 查明这件事的真相。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: At this point, it's Hakeem with certainly the help of NASA opening some doors and starting to really delve into the archives.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，哈基姆在NASA的帮助下打开了一些大门，并开始真正深入查阅档案。

sentences.en: So once empowered to carry out this inquiry, what does Hakeem find?
sentences.zh: 那么一旦获得授权开展这项调查，哈基姆发现了什么？

sentences.en: He starts researching the entire life story of James Webb.
sentences.zh: 他开始研究詹姆斯·韦布的一生。

sentences.en: And he discovers the biography of a lifelong, high-level technocrat.
sentences.zh: 他发现了一位终身为官的高级技术官僚的生平。

sentences.en: And after World War II, Webb was asked by President Harry Truman to go to the State Department and help in what is essentially a global battle with communism.
sentences.zh: 二战后，韦布应总统哈里·杜鲁门的请求前往国务院，协助开展一场本质上针对共产主义的全球斗争。

sentences.en: Webb gets there just as the Red Scare is really taking off in the United States with accusations that many people at the State Department are either communist sympathizers or closet communists.
sentences.zh: 韦布到任时，正值美国的红色恐慌急速升温，许多国务院官员被指控为共产主义同情者或隐蔽的共产党人。

sentences.en: An accusation that could and did destroy the careers of thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可能而且确实毁掉了数千人职业生涯的指控。

sentences.en: Thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It was an absolutely toxic accusation and it destroyed many, many lives.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝对具有毒性的指控，它毁掉了许多人的生活。

sentences.en: Layer on top of that, the Republican senators who were leading the Red Scare also were going after State Department officials as homosexuals.
sentences.zh: 在此之上，领导红色恐慌的共和党参议员还将矛头指向了身为同性恋的国务院官员。

sentences.en: And that was a, you know, sort of a double mark of cane for anyone working at the State Department.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这对于任何在国务院工作的人来说都是一种双重的耻辱标志。

sentences.en: The accusation being that at that time, if you were homosexual, that would have made you sort of doubly susceptible to being blackmailed,
sentences.zh: 当时的指控是，如果你是同性恋，这会使你更容易受到勒索，

sentences.en: to possibly being turned into a double agent.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能变成双重间谍。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I should say there's no proof that this ever happened with anyone, but that was certainly the, in that day and age, the late 1940s, that was the anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我必须说明，没有证据表明这种事在任何人身上发生过，但那确实是那个时代——20世纪40年代末的焦虑所在。

sentences.en: The anxiety, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，那种焦虑。

sentences.en: And this becomes known as the Lavender Scare.
sentences.zh: 这就成了所谓的“薰衣草恐慌”。

sentences.en: And the allegation is that James Webb was a central actor in this controversy, that he really led the prosecution from within the State Department,
sentences.zh: 指控称詹姆斯·韦布是这场争议的核心人物，他实际上领导了国务院内部的起诉工作，

sentences.en: working hand in hand with Republican senators in going after and purging gay employees at the State Department.
sentences.zh: 与共和党参议员携手合作，追查并清洗国务院的同性恋雇员。

sentences.en: And what specific evidence is put forward about Webb's role in this Lavender Scare?
sentences.zh: 关于韦布在这场薰衣草恐慌中所扮演的角色，提出了什么具体证据？

sentences.en: Well, it's twofold.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有两个方面。

sentences.en: One, there's this quote that he allegedly wrote in a government report, and it goes like this.
sentences.zh: 第一，有传言称他在一份政府报告中写过这样一句话，内容大致如下。

sentences.en: It is generally believed that those who engage in overt acts of perversion lack the emotional stability of normal persons.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为，那些参与公开越轨行为的人缺乏正常人的情绪稳定性。

sentences.en: As kind of a justification for forcing out gay workers.
sentences.zh: 作为迫使同性恋员工离开的一种借口。

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The second is that Webb personally fired 91 gay employees from the State Department.
sentences.zh: 第二点是韦布亲自解雇了国务院的91名同性恋员工。

sentences.en: Serious claiMs.
sentences.zh: 严重的指控。

sentences.en: Serious claiMs.
sentences.zh: 严重的指控。

sentences.en: And if true, you can understand very much why people today would look at that with a sense of horror.
sentences.zh: 如果这是真的，你完全可以理解为什么今天的人们会带着一种惊恐的心情来看待这件事。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And what does Hakeem find about all this?
sentences.zh: 哈基姆对这一切有什么发现？

sentences.en: So, he systematically goes about this.
sentences.zh: 所以，他系统性地着手处理此事。

sentences.en: He delves into the NASA archives.
sentences.zh: 他深入查阅了NASA的档案。

sentences.en: He delves into the congressional archives.
sentences.zh: 他深入查阅了国会档案。

sentences.en: And after reading every piece of information on Webb, he still can't find any evidence that Webb wrote this damning, bigoted quote.
sentences.zh: 在阅读了所有关于韦布的信息后，他仍然找不到任何证据证明韦布写过那句带有定罪性质、充满偏见的引文。

sentences.en: But eventually, he does find the quote.
sentences.zh: 但最终，他确实找到了这句话。

sentences.en: And this exact quote that was horrible that was put in his name appeared in a Senate report, not in James Webb's words.
sentences.zh: 而这句挂在他名下的可怕原话实际上出现在参议院的一份报告中，而不是詹姆斯·韦布的原话。

sentences.en: Webb didn't write it.
sentences.zh: 不是韦布写的。

sentences.en: It's actually from a report issued by the Senate that Webb had absolutely nothing to do with.
sentences.zh: 它实际上出自参议院发布的一份报告，而韦布与该报告毫无关系。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What about the second accusation that Webb fired gay employees?
sentences.zh: 关于韦布解雇同性恋员工的第二个指控呢？

sentences.en: It wasn't James Webb.
sentences.zh: 那不是詹姆斯·韦布。

sentences.en: Put simply, he didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，他没有这么做。

sentences.en: So, it was a case of mistaken identity.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一起身份认同错误案件。

sentences.en: That appeared to be the case to me.
sentences.zh: 在我看来情况确实如此。

sentences.en: Everything was done by John Purifor and Carlisle Humelsine.
sentences.zh: 一切都是由约翰·普里弗和卡莱尔·休姆尔辛完成的。

sentences.en: Who were two other employees at the State Department.
sentences.zh: 他们是国务院另外两名雇员。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It was done by other officials at the State Department who were essentially in charge of working with the United States Senate in prosecuting both this red scare and the lavender scare,
sentences.zh: 这是由国务院的其他官员完成的，他们基本上负责与美国参议院合作，起诉红色恐慌和薰衣草恐慌，

sentences.en: the lavender purge.
sentences.zh: 即薰衣草大清洗。

sentences.en: So, in other words, getting rid of people both because they might be communist sympathizers and because they're gay.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，清除那些可能同情共产主义以及身为同性恋的人。

sentences.en: You know, James Webb was the undersecretary of state.
sentences.zh: 要知道，詹姆斯·韦布当时是副国务卿。

sentences.en: They were like deputy undersecretary of state.
sentences.zh: 他们就像是助理副国务卿。

sentences.en: So, what Hakeem has found is that the central allegations that first materialized in those articles he had read a few years earlier and drummed up all this anger at Webb,
sentences.zh: 因此，哈基姆发现，最初出现在他几年前读过的那些文章中并激起对韦布满腔愤怒的核心指控，

sentences.en: that those central allegations are basically not accurate.
sentences.zh: 那些核心指控基本上是不准确的。

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what's also particularly interesting is he finds in looking at Webb's tenure at NASA in the 1960s that Webb had played a key role in helping to racially integrate this massive agency,
sentences.zh: 特别有趣的是，他在研究韦布20世纪60年代在NASA的任职经历时发现，韦布在帮助这个庞大机构实现种族融合方面发挥了关键作用，

sentences.en: particularly at its famed research facilities in Huntsville, Alabama.
sentences.zh: 特别是在其位于阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔的著名研究设施中。

sentences.en: The South.
sentences.zh: 南方。

sentences.en: The South.
sentences.zh: 南方。

sentences.en: And here it's very important to understand historical context.
sentences.zh: 在这里，理解历史背景非常重要。

sentences.en: George Wallace is the arch-segregationist governor of Alabama, absolutely opposed to any idea of integrating federal agencies on his watch in Alabama,
sentences.zh: 乔治·华莱士是阿拉巴马州坚定的种族隔离主义州长，坚决反对在他主政阿拉巴马期间联邦机构实现种族融合的任何想法，

sentences.en: puts a lot of pressure on Webb and President Johnson not to do this.
sentences.zh: 向韦布和约翰逊总统施加了很大压力，要求不要这么做。

sentences.en: And Webb says, no, we're going to integrate this agency.
sentences.zh: 而韦布说，不，我们要让这个机构实现种族融合。

sentences.en: He even, at one point, threatens to move key parts of that facility out of Alabama, which is a strong shot across the bow to Alabama.
sentences.zh: 他甚至在某个时刻威胁要将该设施的关键部门迁出阿拉巴马州，这对阿拉巴马州来说是一个强烈的警告。

sentences.en: Right, and to its extremely prominent and powerful segregationist governor.
sentences.zh: 没错，也是对那位极其显赫且极具权势的种族隔离主义州长的警告。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in the end, George Wallace backed down.
sentences.zh: 最后，乔治·华莱士退让了。

sentences.en: When you come across this and you're told of this background, how does it make you feel?
sentences.zh: 当你遇到这种情况并被告知这段背景时，你作何感想？

sentences.en: I have to be honest in the sense that it did endear me to Webb a little bit to see that he stood up for African-Americans in that way.
sentences.zh: 我必须诚实地说，看到他以那种方式为非裔美国人挺身而出，确实让我对韦布产生了好感。

sentences.en: That was close to my heart.
sentences.zh: 这触动了我的心弦。

sentences.en: NASA, Kennedy, Johnson, Webb, they were doing the right thing.
sentences.zh: NASA、肯尼迪、约翰逊、韦布，他们当时在做正确的事。

sentences.en: So according to Hakeem's research, not only is Webb not a bigot, he is actively working to make the United States government more inclusive.
sentences.zh: 因此，根据哈基姆的研究，韦布不仅不是一个顽固偏狭的人，他还在积极致力于让美国政府更具包容性。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Once I had those two things together, oh, I love Webb now.
sentences.zh: 一旦我把这两点结合起来，哦，我现在太喜欢韦布了。

sentences.en: And what does Hakeem do with this information that clearly undercuts everything that's being said in this moment about James Webb?
sentences.zh: 哈基姆如何处理这些明显削弱了当前对詹姆斯·韦布各种说法的资讯？

sentences.en: Well, first, of course, he goes back and he tells NASA what he's found.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，当然是回到NASA，把他的发现告诉他们。

sentences.en: And then he writes an article in which he lays out at some length all of his findings.
sentences.zh: 然后他写了一篇文章，详细阐述了他的所有发现。

sentences.en: And he's, you know, tough in that piece.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他在那篇文章里写得很严厉。

sentences.en: I mean, he says, look, there have been accusations made by essentially people within my community that is physicists that he is a homophobe and it led this lavender purge.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他说，听着，我的社群（即物理学家）内部的人基本上提出了指控，说他是一个同性恋恐惧症患者，并领导了这场薰衣草大清洗。

sentences.en: And he's saying that's all wrong.
sentences.zh: 而他说这一切都是错的。

sentences.en: And in fact, his article was entitled, was NASA's historic leader, James Webb, a bigot?
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的文章标题是，NASA的历史性领袖詹姆斯·韦布是一个顽固偏狭的人吗？

sentences.en: And can you read me your conclusion?
sentences.zh: 你能给我读一下你的结论吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Let me find it.
sentences.zh: 让找一下。

sentences.en: Hakeem Oluge Webb.
sentences.zh: 哈基姆·奥卢格·韦布。

sentences.en: That'll find it.
sentences.zh: 这样就能找到了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I wrote, in full disclosure, I have never met James Webb, who died in 1992.
sentences.zh: 我写道，坦白来讲，我从未见过1992年去世的詹姆斯·韦布。

sentences.en: I have no idea what was in his heart and mind.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他的内心和想法是什么。

sentences.en: But what I can say conclusively is that there is zero evidence that Webb is guilty of the allegations against him.
sentences.zh: 但我可以确凿地说，没有丝毫证据表明韦布对针对他的指控负有责任。

sentences.en: And he makes very clear no, no, and no.
sentences.zh: 他非常明确地表示：不，不，不。

sentences.en: He's very unequivocal about what he found.
sentences.zh: 对于自己的发现，他的态度非常明确。

sentences.en: When you hit publish on that essay, what did you expect?
sentences.zh: 当你点击发布那篇论文时，你有什么期望？

sentences.en: Did you think there would be blowback?
sentences.zh: 你认为会有强烈反弹吗？

sentences.en: I did not expect blowback.
sentences.zh: 我没想到会有反弹。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: I thought there would be a big sigh of relief from the astronomy community and we'd move forward.
sentences.zh: 我以为天文学界会松一大口气，然后我们就可以继续前进了。

sentences.en: And what was the initial reaction?
sentences.zh: 最初的反应是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the initial reaction was exactly that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最初的反应正是如此。

sentences.en: There was, like, immediately, you know, 400 or so astronomers quote tweeted that article with, hey, now we can move on.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，几乎立刻就有大约400名天文学家引用推特转发了那篇文章，配文是“嘿，现在我们可以继续前进了”。

sentences.en: It's not true.
sentences.zh: 这不是真的。

sentences.en: But then a few days later, things changed drastically.
sentences.zh: 但几天后，情况急转直下。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜卢。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“同义连线”游戏。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天都创作“拼字蜂”和“字里行间”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called Chromesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色彩联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚刚听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: Michael, what does Hakeem mean when he says that the initial reaction to his piece changes drastically?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，哈基姆说对他文章的最初反应发生了巨大变化，这是什么意思？

sentences.en: At first, many physicists look at his article, look at the research, and there's a sense of relief.
sentences.zh: 起初，许多物理学家看了他的文章，看了研究结果，有一种如释重负的感觉。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: We don't have to worry about that.
sentences.zh: 我们不必担心那个了。

sentences.en: We have not named this spectacular telescope after a homophobe.
sentences.zh: 我们没有用一个恐同者名字来命名这个壮观的望远镜。

sentences.en: Then the criticism comes, and it is aimed at Hakeem personally and at his historical research.
sentences.zh: 然后批评声随之而来，矛头直指哈基姆个人以及他的历史研究。

sentences.en: And one of my colleagues, who I had known since 2008, published an article with the title,
sentences.zh: 我的一位自2008年就认识的同事发表了一篇文章，标题是，

sentences.en: The Straights Are Here to Save Us, about me, and this article and his research.
sentences.zh: 《直人来拯救我们》，内容是关于我、这篇文章以及他的研究。

sentences.en: You know, and I'm just like, whoa.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我当时就想，哇。

sentences.en: The first element boils down to who are you, a straight male physicist, to tell us, queer, gay physicists, and employees of NASA and other universities, what Webb was about.
sentences.zh: 核心问题归结为：你一个直男物理学家，凭什么来告诉我们这些酷儿、同性恋物理学家以及NASA和其他大学的员工，韦布究竟是个什么样的人。

sentences.en: Who were you to tell us our history?
sentences.zh: 你凭什么来告诉我们我们的历史？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: This is basically a criticism that Hakeem is not qualified as a non-gay, non-queer person to even carry out this inquiry.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是在批评哈基姆作为一个非同性恋、非酷儿的人，根本没有资格进行这项调查。

sentences.en: Yes, not qualified by dint of his identity.
sentences.zh: 是的，由于他的身份而认为他不具备资格。

sentences.en: You know, and I'm just like, whoa.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我当时就想，哇。

sentences.en: First off, I thought we had a cordial working relationship.
sentences.zh: 首先，我以为我们有着亲切的工作关系。

sentences.en: Why, you know, why are you dissing me like this personally?
sentences.zh: 为什么，你知道的，你为什么要这样人身攻击我？

sentences.en: And what about the historical critique?
sentences.zh: 那历史批判呢？

sentences.en: Because from everything you've said, his research is pretty clear cut and it's pretty compelling.
sentences.zh: 因为根据你所说的一切，他的研究非常明确且相当引人注目。

sentences.en: Well, they say that my research changes nothing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们说我的研究改变不了什么。

sentences.en: All I did was look at a quote and who actually said it, but that was it, right?
sentences.zh: 我所做的只是看了一句话以及是谁实际说出了这句话，仅此而已，对吧？

sentences.en: Look, critics say he missed a few things, including something that happened in the early 1960s when Webb was chief administrator at NASA.
sentences.zh: 听着，批评者说他漏掉了一些事情，包括20世纪60年代初韦布担任NASA行政长官时发生的一件事。

sentences.en: A gay employee at NASA was caught in a sting by police in Washington, D.C., and was later fired by NASA.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿特区一名同性恋NASA员工被警方设局抓获，随后被NASA解雇。

sentences.en: And the accusation was that Webb should have known about this, could have known about this, and should have stopped it.
sentences.zh: 指控是韦布本应该知道这件事，本可以知道这件事，并且本应该阻止它。

sentences.en: Because he ran.
sentences.zh: 因为他是管理者。

sentences.en: Because he ran NASA.
sentences.zh: 因为他掌管着NASA。

sentences.en: And what does Hakeem say about that?
sentences.zh: 哈基姆对此怎么说？

sentences.en: Hakeem points out several things.
sentences.zh: 哈基姆指出了几点。

sentences.en: One is there's no particular reason to think that Webb would have known about this.
sentences.zh: 首先，没有特别的理由认为韦布会知道这件事。

sentences.en: This was not a top employee at NASA.
sentences.zh: 这不是NASA的高层员工。

sentences.en: NASA is a very large federal agency.
sentences.zh: NASA是一个非常大的联邦机构。

sentences.en: But even more to the point, there was an executive order signed by President Eisenhower, and that was enforced for the next 20 years,
sentences.zh: 但更切中要害的是，当时有一项由艾森豪威尔总统签署的行政命令，并在接下来的20年里一直得到执行，

sentences.en: saying that openly gay Americans could not work for the federal government.
sentences.zh: 规定公开的同性恋美国人不得为联邦政府工作。

sentences.en: It was not a NASA policy.
sentences.zh: 这不是NASA的政策。

sentences.en: It was a federal government-wide policy that applied to every federal agency.
sentences.zh: 这是一项适用于所有联邦机构的整个联邦政府层面的政策。

sentences.en: It was wrong-minded.
sentences.zh: 这是思想不端的。

sentences.en: It was wrong-minded.
sentences.zh: 这是思想不端的。

sentences.en: I 100% it was wrong.
sentences.zh: 我百分之百赞同这是错误的。

sentences.en: And there are bad actors, and we know their names.
sentences.zh: 而且确实有坏人，我们也知道他们的名字。

sentences.en: And James Webb is not among them.
sentences.zh: 而詹姆斯·韦布不在其中。

sentences.en: So the relevant context is that Webb may or may not have known about this firing.
sentences.zh: 所以相关的背景是，韦布可能知道也可能不知道这次解雇。

sentences.en: There's no evidence he played a role in it, and that the firing more or less followed the law of the land.
sentences.zh: 没有证据表明他在其中发挥了作用，而且这次解雇多多少少遵循了当时的法律。

sentences.en: Yes, he would have literally had to disobey an executive order by the President of the United States.
sentences.zh: 是的，他实际上必须违抗美国总统的行政命令。

sentences.en: They didn't admit that he didn't do what he was accused of.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有承认他没有做他被指控的事情。

sentences.en: They just said, oh, what Hakeem does not understand is that Webb was complicit because he was in management.
sentences.zh: 他们只是说，哦，哈基姆不明白的是，韦布是共犯，因为他在管理层。

sentences.en: And this gets to this broader critique of Hakeem's work, that James Webb had a responsibility at various places, both when he was at the State Department and when he was at NASA,
sentences.zh: 这就触及了对哈基姆工作的更广泛批评，即詹姆斯·韦布在各个地方都负有责任，无论是在国务院还是在NASA期间，

sentences.en: to speak up for gay rights and to speak up for gay Americans.
sentences.zh: 都要为同性恋权利发声，为同性恋美国人发声。

sentences.en: And that if he failed to do so, he had failed morally, that he had failed in his moral obligation to history.
sentences.zh: 如果他未能做到这一点，那他在道德上就是失败的，他在对历史的道德义务上失败了。

sentences.en: So this is intriguing.
sentences.zh: 所以这很耐人寻味。

sentences.en: This criticism of Hakeem's research is that whether or not Webb himself did any of the things he'd been accused of doing, which Hakeem has found he didn't,
sentences.zh: 对哈基姆研究的这种批评是，无论韦布本人是否做了他被指控的那些事——哈基姆发现他并没有做——

sentences.en: the fact that as a leader, he didn't do more to stop it makes him worthy of condemnation.
sentences.zh: 作为一个领导者，他没有采取更多行动去阻止这件事，这一事实本身就让他理应受到谴责。

sentences.en: Yes, precisely.
sentences.zh: 是的，确切地说。

sentences.en: There's a word in historiography, presentism, which is this idea that one can apply the moral lens of our current day to past events.
sentences.zh: 史学中有一个词叫“现在主义”，即把我们当代的道德视角应用于过去事件的观点。

sentences.en: I mean, it's raised around our civil war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在我们的内战中经常被提出。

sentences.en: It's raised around any kind of really urgent, certainly the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 在任何真正紧迫的事情周围都会被提出，当然也包括民权运动。

sentences.en: In this case, it would be applied to James Webb and saying, look, in 1949, 1950, when you're at the State Department and gay employees or potentially gay employees,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，它将被应用于詹姆斯·韦布，并说，看，在1949、1950年，当你担任国务院职务时，同性恋员工或潜在的同性恋员工——

sentences.en: because no one quite knows who they are, are coming under attack.
sentences.zh: 因为没有人十分清楚他们是谁——正受到攻击。

sentences.en: That you should have understood this as a moral civil rights issue and stood up and said something and resign if you needed to.
sentences.zh: 你应该将此理解为一个道德民权问题，站出来说点什么，如果需要的话甚至可以辞职。

sentences.en: Let me give you an example.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个例子。

sentences.en: There's a professor at the University of New Hampshire, Dr. Chanda Prescott Weinstein, a well-known physiciSt.
sentences.zh: 新罕布什尔大学有一位教授，查达·普雷斯科特-韦恩斯坦博士，是一位著名的物理学家。

sentences.en: She's been very critical of Hakeem, and she argues that James Webb, in fact, had a choice that, as she wrote,
sentences.zh: 她对哈基姆一直持严厉批评态度，她认为詹姆斯·韦布实际上是有选择的，正如她所写的那样，

sentences.en: he could have been a radical freedom fighter and simply refused to serve in the Truman administration.
sentences.zh: 他本可以成为一个激进的自由斗士，简单地拒绝在杜鲁门政府中任职。

sentences.en: So how should we think about an argument like that?
sentences.zh: 那我们该如何看待这样的论点呢？

sentences.en: Well, the problem is that if you talk to historians, including some very prominent gay historians who've studied this period, I mean,
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题在于，如果你跟历史学家谈谈，包括一些研究过这一时期的非常杰出的同性恋历史学家，我的意思是，

sentences.en: there was not a gay rights movement at that time.
sentences.zh: 当时根本没有什么同性恋权利运动。

sentences.en: Presentism, in this sort of a case, is seen as asking people to anticipate where history is moving in a way that is simply kind of beyond their kin at that time.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，“现在主义”被视为要求人们去预见历史将走向何方，而这在当时完全超出了他们的认知范围。

sentences.en: to have expected essentially someone to intuit that there would be a gay rights movement that would arise in the next two and three and four decades and come to flower is not reasonable.
sentences.zh: 实质上要求某人直觉地预感到未来两、三、四十年内会兴起一场同性恋权利运动并最终开花结果，这是不合理的。

sentences.en: That is their argument.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的论点。

sentences.en: Michael, no matter what intellectual framework you subscribe to when it comes to James Webb,
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，无论你赞同关于詹姆斯·韦布的哪种知识框架，

sentences.en: it feels like what has happened in the case of Hakeem's research is that an original critique has been transformed and changed.
sentences.zh: 感觉在哈基姆的研究中发生的事情是，最初的批判已经被转化和改变了。

sentences.en: And in a sense, the goalposts have moved.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，目标被移动了。

sentences.en: First, the accusation was that he did something very wrong.
sentences.zh: 首先，指控是他做了一件非常错误的事。

sentences.en: That was disproven, and so the critique transforms into he was complicit.
sentences.zh: 这一点被推翻了，于是批判转变为他是同谋。

sentences.en: So how does Hakeem start to think about that?
sentences.zh: 那么哈基姆是如何开始思考这一点的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, Hakeem finds himself frustrated, frankly, at this shifting of the argument from one thing to the next to the next.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，坦率地说，哈基姆发现自己感到沮丧，因为这种争论从一件事变到另一件事，再变到又一件事。

sentences.en: They started with he initiated it, he's a homophobe.
sentences.zh: 他们从他发起这件事开始，说他是个恐同者。

sentences.en: Then they pull back to he's complicit.
sentences.zh: 然后他们退回到他是同谋。

sentences.en: Then they get a hint of something.
sentences.zh: 然后他们又捕风捉影。

sentences.en: It's never quite clear where this ends.
sentences.zh: 永远也搞不清楚这到底什么时候是个头。

sentences.en: And at some point, Hakeem, a scientist, a man who loves to research, starts to realize, you know, facts are probably not going to be the end of this.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，哈基姆，一个科学家，一个热爱研究的人，开始意识到，你知道，事实可能无法彻底终结这一切。

sentences.en: You know, there's not going to be one finding, one set of facts that is kind of going to put this to reSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不会有一个发现、一套能够让这一切平息的事实。

sentences.en: So sometimes the truth of the data is so obvious, but because of politics or some other reason, people will claim that they don't see what is obvious.
sentences.zh: 所以有时数据的真相是如此明显，但由于政治或其他原因，人们会声称他们看不到显而易见的事情。

sentences.en: And that's why this episode feels very relevant to our current cultural moment.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这个插曲让我们感觉与当前的文化时刻息息相关。

sentences.en: And there is, I think, indisputably a growing tendency by progressive forces in our culture to revisit the past with disapproving eyes.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，在我们文化中的进步力量中，用不赞同的眼光重新审视过去的倾向无疑在日益增加。

sentences.en: It often comes from a place of justifiable anger over a historical wrong, but at times it can seem uninterested and pretty unforgiving of the values that existed in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 它通常源于对历史错误的合理愤怒，但有时它似乎对过去存在的价值观不感兴趣且极其严苛。

sentences.en: And it can be dismissive of the facts and the nuances that don't conform to the ultimate judgments of those who disapprove of it.
sentences.zh: 并且它可能会对那些不符合反对者最终判断的事实和细微差别不屑一顾。

sentences.en: Does that feel right?
sentences.zh: 感觉是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I see this all the time in my writing and reporting and in talking with Hakeem.
sentences.zh: 我在我的写作、报道以及与哈基姆的交谈中一直看到这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, he confronted, in a sense, the conundrum, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从某种意义上说，他面临着这个难题，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, on the one hand, it's enormously frustrating to see facts ignored or perhaps shunned aside.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一方面，看到事实被忽视或被抛在一边，是极其令人沮丧的。

sentences.en: On the other hand, as he talks about himself, he gets it.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，正如他自己所说的那样，他理解。

sentences.en: He gets this sense of pain and aggrievement as you look back at history and try to make sense of history.
sentences.zh: 当你回首历史并试图理解历史时，他理解这种痛苦和愤慨的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, when I first saw this, I thought about, what if it was me?
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我第一次看到这个时，我想到了，如果是我呢？

sentences.en: What if I lived in my town and there was this Confederate statue?
sentences.zh: 如果我住在我的小镇里，那里有这样一座邦联雕像呢？

sentences.en: And this dude, not only was he Confederate, he was like an overseer and a murderer of African people who were enslaved back then.
sentences.zh: 而这个家伙，不仅是个邦联支持者，他还是当年被奴役的非洲人民的监工和杀手。

sentences.en: This is what I think my whole life.
sentences.zh: 我一辈子都是这么想的。

sentences.en: And now this white dude in the community goes and does the research and says, hey, you know what?
sentences.zh: 现在社区里的这个白人家伙去做了研究，然后说，嘿，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Turns out it wasn't that guy.
sentences.zh: 事实证明根本不是那个人。

sentences.en: He didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 他没有做过那件事。

sentences.en: And as a matter of fact, he saved the lives of hundreds of Native Americans.
sentences.zh: 而且事实上，他还拯救了数百名美洲原住民的生命。

sentences.en: I would be in no hurry to unhate that guy, right?
sentences.zh: 我可不会急着停止去恨那个家伙，对吧？

sentences.en: If all this time I thought that dude was that evil person, even when I found the truth, I still would feel some kind of way.
sentences.zh: 如果这么长时间以来我一直认为那家伙是个恶魔，即使我发现了真相，我心里还是会有某种感觉。

sentences.en: That's a natural feeling.
sentences.zh: 这是一种自然的情感。

sentences.en: I get that.
sentences.zh: 我理解这一点。

sentences.en: So what ends up happening next in Hakeem's story?
sentences.zh: 那么哈基姆的故事接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: It takes a decidedly nasty and personal turn.
sentences.zh: 它朝着坚决恶劣和人身攻击的方向发展。

sentences.en: He is offered a job at George Mason University and there is an accusation.
sentences.zh: 他得到了乔治·梅森大学的一份工作，随之而来的是一项指控。

sentences.en: What I heard people were saying was that I had sexually harassed a woman at my university.
sentences.zh: 我听到别人说的是，我在我所在的大学性骚扰了一名女性。

sentences.en: I was at Florida Tech and that in my federal grants that I received that I had absconded with federal money, that I had stolen money.
sentences.zh: 我曾在佛罗里达理工学院工作，在我获得的联邦资助中，我携款潜逃了，我偷了钱。

sentences.en: These accusations are made in a roundabout way on Twitter and in a phone call to another physics professor at George Mason University who properly takes them to the administration at George Mason.
sentences.zh: 这些指控是通过绕弯子的方式在推特上提出的，并且通过电话打给了乔治·梅森大学的另一位物理学教授，而这位教授妥善地将这些情况反映给了乔治·梅森的行政部门。

sentences.en: And George Mason in turn gets in touch with the Florida Institute of Technology.
sentences.zh: 乔治·梅森大学反过来又联系了佛罗里达理工学院。

sentences.en: It's very important to note that there is no there there.
sentences.zh: 非常重要的一点是要指出，这件事根本纯属子虚乌有。

sentences.en: Florida Institute of Technology had investigated these accusations a couple of years earlier and reinvestigated those, found nothing there.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达理工学院在几年前就已经调查过这些指控，并重新进行了调查，发现根本没有这回事。

sentences.en: I spent a good three weeks of reporting time trying to track down these allegations, talking to many former students, and I could find nothing.
sentences.zh: 我花了好三周的报道时间试图追查这些指控，与许多前学生交谈，结果什么也没找到。

sentences.en: And nor did Florida Institute of Technology, nor did George Mason, which went ahead with its hire.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达理工学院没有找到，乔治·梅森大学也没有找到，后者继续推进了聘用流程。

sentences.en: And in fact, Hakeem Olusheye is now a visiting professor at George Mason.
sentences.zh: 事实上，哈基姆·奥卢谢耶现在是乔治·梅森大学的访问教授。

sentences.en: I have to point out something that I'm sure occurred to you, Michael, while you were reporting this, which is at this point in the story,
sentences.zh: 我必须指出一件事，迈克尔，当你做这篇报道时，我确信你也想到了，那就是在故事的这个阶段，

sentences.en: you're looking into the reputation of someone who was attacked after looking into the reputation of someone else who was attacked.
sentences.zh: 你在调查一个在调查了另一个被攻击的人之后自己也遭到攻击的人的名誉。

sentences.en: And perhaps all these attacks are coming from the same set of sources.
sentences.zh: 也许所有这些攻击都来自同一批消息来源。

sentences.en: Yes, this is the politics of personal destruction that accompany so many disputes these days where one challenges the consensus around a particular issue.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是伴随着如今许多争端的毁灭个人名誉的政治，在这些争端中，人们对围绕某一特定问题的共识提出挑战。

sentences.en: And it's not enough to argue with that, to say, no, no, no, you're wrong because of X, Y, and Z.
sentences.zh: 仅仅反驳这一点是不够的，不能说，不，不，不，因为A、B、C，所以你是错的。

sentences.en: You need to take that person down and personal reputations are destroyed.
sentences.zh: 你需要把那个人搞垮，个人名誉就这样被摧毁了。

sentences.en: It's an unfortunately common aspect of intellectual debate these days.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这是如今知识界辩论中一个常见的方面。

sentences.en: So we know how this story ends, of course.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当然知道这个故事的结局。

sentences.en: The James Webb Space Telescope is up in the skies.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·韦布太空望远镜已经升入太空。

sentences.en: We know it is named the James Webb Space Telescope.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它被命名为詹姆斯·韦布太空望远镜。

sentences.en: But has NASA itself ever officially weighed in on this entire saga and debate about Webb and about his past?
sentences.zh: 但是NASA本身是否曾就关于韦布及其过去的整个传奇和辩论正式发表过意见？

sentences.en: Yes, they have.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们发表过。

sentences.en: Their in-house historian did a quite complete report that essentially ratified everything Hakeem had found.
sentences.zh: 他们的内部历史学家写了一份相当完整的报告，基本上证实了哈基姆发现的一切。

sentences.en: Now, the report's very careful.
sentences.zh: 现在，这份报告非常谨慎。

sentences.en: History's complicated, right?
sentences.zh: 历史很复杂，对吧？

sentences.en: We can't know with 100% certainty what James Webb really believed in his heart.
sentences.zh: 我们无法百分之百确定地知道詹姆斯·韦布内心真正相信什么。

sentences.en: But the report goes through every accusation against him.
sentences.zh: 但这份报告逐一反驳了针对他的每一项指控。

sentences.en: And the historical record just doesn't back those up.
sentences.zh: 历史记录根本不支持这些指控。

sentences.en: So where is Hakeem right now in his career?
sentences.zh: 那么哈基姆目前的职业生涯进展如何？

sentences.en: And has any of this in his mind changed his life, changed his trajectory?
sentences.zh: 这一切在他的心中是否改变了他的生活，改变了他的轨迹？

sentences.en: I think when one goes through a crucible like this, and it was a crucible for Hakeem in his telling,
sentences.zh: 我认为当一个人经历这样严峻的考验时——用他自己的话说，这对哈基姆来说确实是一场严峻的考验——

sentences.en: it certainly has left him with a sense of precisely how fraught and charged our cultural moment is.
sentences.zh: 这无疑让他真切地感受到我们的文化时刻是多么充满压力和充满火药味。

sentences.en: But when I've asked him, if you could go back, knowing what you know now, would you still do this?
sentences.zh: 但当我问他，如果时光倒流，以你现在的了解，你还会这么做吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd definitely do it again.
sentences.zh: 是的，我绝对还会再做一次。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there's not a regret for having looked into this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，对于去调查这件事，我一点也不后悔。

sentences.en: I mean, I think he feels that he did what he felt he had an intellectual obligation to do, which was to look at these charges as clearly as he could and come to some conclusions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得他做了他觉得自己有知识义务去做的事情，那就是尽可能清晰地审视这些指控并得出一些结论。

sentences.en: That turned out to be right.
sentences.zh: 事实证明那是正确的。

sentences.en: That turned out to be right.
sentences.zh: 事实证明那是正确的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I had no personal connection to James Webb.
sentences.zh: 我与詹姆斯·韦布没有任何个人联系。

sentences.en: There was nothing that made me want to exonerate James Webb.
sentences.zh: 没有任何东西让我想要为詹姆斯·韦布开脱。

sentences.en: There was nothing that made me feel like I could somehow gain an advantage from doing this.
sentences.zh: 没有任何东西让我觉得通过这样做我可以从中捞到什么好处。

sentences.en: If anything, I knew that there was only a downside.
sentences.zh: 如果要说有什么的话，我知道这只有坏处。

sentences.en: There was nothing in it for me, period.
sentences.zh: 我从中得不到任何好处，句号。

sentences.en: But once I found out the truth, I was now bound to reveal that truth.
sentences.zh: 但是一旦我发现了真相，我现在就有义务揭露这个真相。

sentences.en: It's my duty.
sentences.zh: 这是我的职责。

sentences.en: It's my responsibility.
sentences.zh: 这是我的责任。

sentences.en: My honor could have it no other way.
sentences.zh: 我的荣誉不容许我有别的选择。

sentences.en: You know, in reflecting on this whole saga, you have to imagine that there are other consensuses, that's the right word out there, that aren't right.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在反思整个传奇时，你必须想象还有其他的共识——用这个词很合适——并不是正确的。

sentences.en: You know, other moments where lots of people think that a James Webb, someone like that, did wrong.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在其他时刻，许多人认为詹姆斯·韦布这样的人做错了事。

sentences.en: But there isn't a Hakeem-like figure devoting the time and, in this case, reputational cost to challenging those narratives because it's just not worth it for them, as we can see.
sentences.zh: 但并没有像哈基姆这样的人物去投入时间和（在本案中）名誉成本来挑战这些叙事，因为正如我们所见，对他们来说这根本不值得。

sentences.en: And so, in that sense, it strikes me that Hakeem's story is inspiring, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，从这个意义上说，我觉得哈基姆的故事是鼓舞人心的，对吧？

sentences.en: The lengths he went, the years he devoted to it, the risks he was willing to tolerate.
sentences.zh: 他付出的努力，他投入的年华，他愿意承受的风险。

sentences.en: Or it's a kind of extreme cautionary tale because who wants to endure all of that just to correct the record for some dead guy, right?
sentences.zh: 或者这是一个某种极端的警示故事，因为谁愿意为了给某个死人澄清记录而忍受这一切呢，对吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And, in fact, in my reporting, I talked to many physicists who did not want to go on the record talking about this.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我的报道中，我采访了许多物理学家，他们不愿意公开谈论这件事。

sentences.en: They said to me, you know, Hakeem got it right and I ain't going there because if I go there, I'm going to get attacked.
sentences.zh: 他们对我说，你知道，哈基姆是对的，但我可不蹚这浑水，因为如果我蹚了，我就会遭到攻击。

sentences.en: And one hears this, frankly, all the time in academia.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，在学术界人们总是听到这样的话。

sentences.en: And I know that there are those, you know, a number of very prominent, you know, liberal scholars and activists who say that this doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 我知道有些人——许多非常杰出的自由派学者和活动家——说这种事不会发生。

sentences.en: But I'm just saying, like, I'm in those conversations.
sentences.zh: 但我只是想说，听着，我身处这些对话之中。

sentences.en: And when you say this is happening, what you mean is a form of fear and self-censorship that makes people fear articulating the truth.
sentences.zh: 当你宣称这种事正在发生时，你的意思是存在一种恐惧和自我审查的形式，让人们不敢说出真相。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, to that view, right.
sentences.zh: 所以，从那种观点来看，对吧。

sentences.en: Hakeem Olusheye is either an inspiring tale of an intellectual who stood up for what he believed in and what he had found.
sentences.zh: 哈基姆·奥卢谢耶要么是一个知识分子坚持自己信仰和所发现真理的鼓舞人心的故事，

sentences.en: Or he's a cautionary tale, as you say, of where you don't want to go.
sentences.zh: 要么正如你所说，是一个你不愿涉足的警示故事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, the other way to think of this entire story, Michael, is that the people who are mad about the Webb telescope from the start were making a larger point.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，看待整个故事的另一个角度是，从一开始就对韦布望远镜感到愤怒的人是在表达一个更大的观点。

sentences.en: And that a factual error here and there, a reputation that maybe gets trampled,
sentences.zh: 这里的某个事实错误，或者可能被践踏的名誉，

sentences.en: isn't ultimately as important as communicating a message about fairness and equality within an institution like the State Department or NASA.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，并不如在国务院或NASA这样的机构内部传达关于公平和平等的讯息那么重要。

sentences.en: And that you don't make omelets without breaking eggs.
sentences.zh: 不打破鸡蛋就做不成煎蛋卷。

sentences.en: You don't change the world without occasionally bruising people.
sentences.zh: 不偶尔伤害到别人就无法改变世界。

sentences.en: Yeah, I suppose if you're not the egg being broken, that's perhaps a more comfortable position.
sentences.zh: 对，我想如果你不是那个被打破的鸡蛋的话，那可能是一个更舒适的位置。

sentences.en: But I think it's fair to say that we venture into dangerous waters if we say that, well, truth can be sacrificed for a greater good.
sentences.zh: 但我认为公平地说，如果我们说真相可以为了更大的利益而牺牲，我们就涉足了危险的领域。

sentences.en: It seems to me, in looking at the life of Hakeem Olusheye, you see the downside risk pretty profoundly.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，回顾哈基姆·奥卢谢耶的生活，你会深刻地看到潜在的巨大风险。

sentences.en: Well, Michael, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，迈克尔，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The Times reports that Senator Dianne Feinstein of California, whose prolonged absence imperiled Democrats' agenda in Congress,
sentences.zh: 据《泰晤士报》报道，加利福尼亚州参议员黛安娜·范斯坦因长期缺席而危及了民主党人在国会的议程，

sentences.en: has returned to work despite a set of serious medical setbacks that have left her in poor health.
sentences.zh: 尽管遭遇了一系列严重的健康挫折导致其身体状况不佳，她还是回到了工作岗位。

sentences.en: Feinstein was first hospitalized with shingles in February, which spread to her face and neck, causing vision and balance impairments and facial paralysis.
sentences.zh: 范斯坦最初于2月因带状疱疹住院，病情扩散至面部和颈部，导致视力和平衡受损以及面瘫。

sentences.en: At the same time, it brought on an undisclosed case of encephalitis, a swelling of the brain that can cause memory loss, language problems, and bouts of confusion.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，它引发了一起未公开的脑炎病例，这是一种会导致记忆力减退、语言障碍和间歇性神志不清的大脑肿胀。

sentences.en: The new information suggests Feinstein was unready to resume work and is now struggling to function in the job.
sentences.zh: 新信息表明，范斯坦尚未准备好恢复工作，目前在胜任工作方面举步维艰。

sentences.en: And Disney is pulling the plug on a $1 billion office complex in Florida,
sentences.zh: 迪士尼正在取消在佛罗里达州投资10亿美元的办公综合体项目，

sentences.en: following a set of relentless politically motivated attacks on the company by the state's Republican governor, Ron DeSantis.
sentences.zh: 此前，该州共和党州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯对该公司进行了持续不断的政治动机攻击。

sentences.en: The office complex would have brought more than 2,000 jobs to the region, with an average salary of $120,000.
sentences.zh: 该办公综合体原本会为该地区带来2000多个工作岗位，平均薪资为12万美元。

sentences.en: Disney's decision highlights the economic risks of DeSantis' presidential aspirations.
sentences.zh: 迪士尼的决定凸显了德桑蒂斯总统野心所带来的经济风险。

sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个被严密控制的机器一样运作。
